title: No violation on a generalisation of Leggett-Garg inequality and Bell-CHSH inequality with extended probability
abstract: A generalisation of the Leggett-Garg inequality (LGI) and the Bell-CHSH inequality is proposed in this work, by replacing a classical probability notion with an extended probability notion. The extended probability serves as an underlying layer of reality to the classical probability. Within the consistent history framework, the underlying layer is so-called a non-settleable history. Hence, the bounds of the LGIs and Bell-CHSH inequalities are extended. The resulting generalised inequalities are satisfied without violation for arbitrary measurement settings. Furthermore, generalised Macro- realism and generalised Local realism are introduced and analysed within the extended probability framework without relying on an explicit measurement. This opens up further possibilities on one of the great pursuits in physics, understanding on how a quantum system can possess classical properties.
summary: This theoretical work generalizes the Leggett-Garg and Bell-CHSH inequalities by replacing classical probability with an 'extended probability' notion derived from non-settleable quantum histories. The main finding is that these generalized inequalities are satisfied without violation, suggesting that quantum systems can exhibit generalized macro-realism and local realism within this extended framework. It provides a mathematical tool to explore the boundary between quantum and classical descriptions of reality.
main_problem: The paper addresses the fundamental challenge of reconciling quantum mechanical predictions with classical notions of reality, specifically concerning the violation of Bell-CHSH and Leggett-Garg inequalities.
main_result: By employing an extended probability framework based on non-settleable histories, the generalized LGI and Bell-CHSH inequalities are shown to be satisfied without violation for arbitrary measurement settings.
method: The authors generalize classical probability by introducing an 'extended probability' notion within the Consistent History framework, allowing for the analysis of underlying, non-observable histories.
model_or_system: The analysis is performed on general quantum systems, testing temporal correlations (LGI) and spatial correlations (Bell-CHSH) using the consistent history formalism.
key_observables: Generalized Leggett-Garg Inequality (gLGI) and generalized Bell-CHSH inequality bounds, along with generalized Macro-realism and Local realism.
important_parameters: The extended probability $q(\alpha)$ and the unsharpness parameter $\eta$ are key mathematical constructs.
main_assumptions: The core assumption is that the underlying layer of reality is the 'non-settleable history,' and the framework relies on the consistent history formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the satisfaction of generalized bounds (gLGI and Bell-CHSH) using extended probability, showing no violation, and demonstrate the reduction of extended unity based on measurement parameters.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the extended probability concept, derives generalized inequalities for LGI and Bell-CHSH, analyzes the implications for generalized realism (gMR/gLR), and discusses the role of counterfactual definiteness.
why_interesting: This work tackles foundational questions about quantum realism and determinism using advanced probability theory, which is crucial for understanding the limits of classical intuition in quantum physics.
